wiki_text: In 2025 the long-stalled Clifton Pier LNG project was revived and entered construction under a Shell + FOCOL Holdings joint venture operating as New Providence Gas (NPG). The Bahamas government signed a terminal development agreement with NPG and an LNG supply agreement with Shell in spring 2025. Combined Phase 1 and Phase 2 construction cost is put at just under US$200 million. The design comprises an offshore jetty platform at Clifton Pier with a pipeline to shore, a Floating Storage Unit (FSU) stationed at the jetty, and 8-16 land-based LNG storage tanks in Phase 1. Nikkiso Clean Energy & Industrial Gases was contracted (Aug 2025) to supply a complete packaged regasification system rated at 55 million scf/day (~0.42 mtpa), including pumps, a gas-fired water-bath vaporizer, controls and vacuum-jacketed pipeline. FOCOL Holdings signed terminal construction with Turner Industries. Government-approved dredging began before the end of August 2025, with excavation and civil works under way. The phased rollout pairs the terminal with 60 MW (rising to 130 MW) of LNG power at Clifton Pier; BPL targeted first LNG engines online in Q1 2026 once the terminal is completed. The project supersedes the 2024 'Blue Hills' pivot that had briefly shelved a Clifton Pier regas facility.

By late 2025 the Island Power Producers (IPP) mini-LNG terminal at Nassau Cruise Port had advanced from award to financing. INOXCVA (INOX India) holds the turnkey EPC contract (awarded Nov 2024) to design, engineer and supply the receiving and regasification terminal, comprising 10 double-walled vacuum-insulated tanks of 1,500 m3 each (15,000 m3 total) - described as the world's largest installation of shop-built vacuum-insulated LNG tanks - feeding IPP's 60 MW combined-cycle plant that will provide shore power to cruise ships. The broader delivery consortium reported in Nov 2025 includes Nassau Cruise Port, Arawak Port Development Company, Crowley (LNG shipping/transport) and Siemens (generation equipment and plant operations). To fund the ~US$179m project, IPP launched a US$100m bond offering on 6 Nov 2025 atop a US$25m loan facility. Phase 1 was targeted for completion by end of Q3 2026 with shore-power operations by end-2026; the Phase 2 steam turbine is scheduled for Q2 2027. The terminal remained in the 'proposed' (pre-construction) stage at the time of these reports.
